clue.text: Partners in most senior 14 play the field

parts.note: the longest royal marriage was that of Prince Philip and Queen Elizabeth, so the partners are Phil and ER (Elizabeth Regina)
the joining word between the two partners' names is taken as it stands
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A couple in the senior royal match are said to stray from each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is ROYAL MARRIAGE; the most senior one was Philip and Elizabeth's, giving PHIL AND ER as a phrase. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a crossword staple for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to flirt or have casual affairs, which is what playing the field means as an idiom.

clue.text: Leading lady, Queen surrounded by diverse signs of empire

indicators.note: the queen is enclosed by the other letters
diverse means varied, so the letters of the word are given in another order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for the Queen

explanation.surface: A leading lady describes the Queen encircled by the trappings of empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverse signs of' rearranges EMPIRE as PREMIE; 'surrounded by' puts ER (Elizabeth Regina) inside it. 'Leading lady' reads as a person, but the French word for a leading actress is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Première can denote the principal actress in French theatre, the female counterpart of premier.

clue.text: Runs out of sarcastic type of bond

indicators.note: the runs abbreviation is taken out of the synonym for sarcastic

parts.note: ironic is a near-synonym of sarcastic
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone stops making cutting remarks and forms a connection.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for runs in cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: An ionic bond in chemistry joins atoms by the attraction of oppositely charged ions.

clue.text: We won't forget being in 23

parts.note: the saying that elephants never forget, spoken by the beasts native to the country that is 23-down

explanation.surface: Natives of a country declare they will always remember.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is INDIA; the proverb says an elephant never forgets.
explanation.definitionFit: The species native to India and its region is famed for long memory, as the old proverb about elephants has it.

clue.text: A classic pain in the neck?

definitions.text: A classic pain in the neck?

parts.words: A classic pain in the neck?
parts.note: the idiom for an annoying person read literally: a famous fictional vampire who bites the neck

explanation.surface: Someone describes a timelessly irritating person.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's vampire count is a literary classic who literally causes neck pain by biting.

clue.text: A scale of shifting temperature in more productive surroundings

indicators.note: the more productive word surrounds the temperature letter

parts.note: richer, as in richer soil, means more fertile or productive

explanation.surface: A gauge records temperature changes in a fertile environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' is part of the definition: the scale measures the earth shifting in quakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Richter scale measures the magnitude of earthquakes, the shifting of the ground.

clue.text: Dress a film star for the main part

indicators.note: only most of the name is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A screen actress is clothed in a costume for her leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the main part' looks like a role in a film, but it says to take most of the star's name: GARBO loses its last letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, a synonym of dress as a noun.

clue.text: Spanning time, adults wobble unsteadily when weak

indicators.note: the adults bridge across time, sitting on either side of it

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: something unsteady wobbles, so the word's letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Old people totter shakily when they are frail.
explanation.walkthrough: AA (adults) spans T to make ATA; 'unsteadily' rearranges WOBBLE as LOWEBB.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a low ebb means being in a weak or depressed state, like a tide at its lowest point.

clue.text: Improve one interested in turf?

definitions.meaning: to make something ..., as a verb
a punter who bets on horse racing, the turf

explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate something is to make it superior, and a gambler on horse races is one who places wagers.

clue.text: On which we're driven, by George

definitions.text: On which we're driven, by George

parts.words: On which we're driven, by George
parts.note: a system that steers a vehicle for us, which pilots nickname George; the exclamation 'by George' disguises that

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about being chauffeured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is old aviation slang for the autopilot, hidden in the exclamation 'by George'.
explanation.definitionFit: Autopilot steers a craft without human control, and was nicknamed George by airmen.

clue.text: Play endless tunes in the doldrums

indicators.note: to play with letters is to toy with their order, so what follows is rearranged
the word tunes loses its ends, leaving only the middle letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to escape boredom by playing music on repeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips T and S from TUNES to leave UNE; add IN, and 'Play' rearranges UNEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doldrums is a state of listless boredom, which is exactly what ennui names.

clue.text: Well up in gold palace without article

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the palace word wraps around the article

parts.note: a royal court is a palace or residence of a sovereign
an is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: A golden palace is described as lacking a certain item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside, so the palace word wraps the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well up in a subject means being fully informed and up to date, the sense of the French borrowing.

clue.text: Halves of thin taco on menu unknown abroad

indicators.note: the second half of each listed word is taken and the pieces run together

explanation.surface: Half a thin taco on the menu turns out to be a mystery dish from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The second halves are IN (thin), CO (taco), N (on) and NU (menu).
explanation.definitionFit: In French an inconnu is an unknown person, so 'abroad' flags the foreign word for a stranger.

clue.text: Brace lowermost spasms after both sides split

indicators.note: spasms are jerky convulsions, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
both sides are left and right, L and R, and once they have split off the rest of the word remains

explanation.surface: Someone braces themselves as the lowest muscles spasm and split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after both sides split' takes L and R (left and right) out of LOWERMOST, leaving OWEMOST, which 'spasms' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair, as of game birds, and a twosome is likewise a pair.

clue.text: Like Marines and Air Force, bombarded grim area for King and Queen at table?

parts.note: both British services are prefixed Royal: the Royal Marines and the Royal Air Force

indicators.note: a bombarded place is blasted apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: Military forces shell a bleak region of battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games such as bezique, a king and queen of trumps held together is called a royal marriage; the question mark flags the card-table sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedded king and queen form a regal union, and at the card table the matched king-queen pair takes the same name.

clue.text: Making off-peak calls?

parts.note: off-peak suggests cheap phone calls, but read as calls sung out from mountain peaks in the Alps

explanation.surface: Someone is phoning at the cheaper time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine herders sing with rapid shifts of pitch from the mountaintops.

clue.text: See gross, awful women?

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look at some dreadful, crude women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges SEE GROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are female monsters of folklore, the feminine of giant man-eaters.

clue.text: Discreet woman, unattractive sort, that can slip past customs?

parts.note: being diplomatic means being tactful and discreet
an old bag is an insulting term for an unattractive woman

explanation.surface: A tactful but unprepossessing woman smuggles something through the border.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch carried for an embassy is protected by diplomatic immunity and is not searched at the border.

clue.text: Unyoke, being sat upon after a bumpy ride

indicators.note: letters that have been bumped about are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone unharnesses a horse after being sat on through a rough journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a bumpy ride' rearranges SAT UPON.
explanation.definitionFit: Outspan is a South African word for unharnessing oxen from a wagon.

clue.text: One worthless badge, turned out in silver

indicators.note: the rearranged badge goes inside the silver symbol

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: turned out means reshaped, so the letters of the word are reordered

explanation.surface: A useless emblem is found remade in silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges BADGE as BADEG; 'in' then places it inside the silver symbol. 'One worthless' is the definition, not a count of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a rotter, a person of no worth.

clue.text: People showing intelligence in dress, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things backwards, so the word is read right to left
the intelligence measure goes inside the dress

parts.note: a sari is a South Asian woman's draped dress
IQ is the intelligence quotient

explanation.surface: People displaying brains in their clothing, when they think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the intelligence measure inside the dress, making SIQARI, and 'on reflection' turns that around; the phrase looks like 'after thinking it over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraqis are a nationality, the inhabitants of a country.

clue.text: Faithful priest engaged in diatribe

indicators.note: the priest is held within the rant, as if occupied inside it

parts.note: a rant is a long angry speech, a diatribe
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A devout clergyman launches into a furious tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI, the biblical priest, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful and reliant are both used of trusting or depending on someone.

clue.text: Inform one paper's to be reprinted

indicators.note: a reprint resets the type, so these letters are set again in a fresh order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
read as plural papers, the letters including the S

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor announces that an edition will be printed again.
explanation.walkthrough: One is I, and PAPERS takes the apostrophe-s as its plural ending; rearranging IPAPERS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to tell them of something, a synonym of inform.

clue.text: Endless raiding ruined country

indicators.note: a ruined thing is wrecked, so the remaining letters are put into disorder
the word loses both of its outer letters, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: Ceaseless raids have devastated a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' strips R and G from RAIDING to leave AIDIN, which 'ruined' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the large South Asian nation, the subcontinent's largest state.

clue.text: Unique plot overthrown-ring off five times

indicators.note: a toppled plot is turned upside down, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the ring-shaped letter comes off the fodder before it is jumbled

parts.note: O resembles a ring in shape

explanation.surface: A singular conspiracy is defeated after a ring of plotters is dispersed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes O (ring) from UNIQUE PLOT, and 'overthrown' rearranges the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintuple means fivefold, multiplied by five.

clue.text: Where you'd immerse in liquid from molten solid

indicators.note: something molten has melted, so the letters of the word lose their fixed form

explanation.surface: A solid melts into liquid and you could bathe in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'molten' signals rearranging SOLID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lidos are public open-air swimming pools, places for a dip in water.

clue.text: Give name to twins, for example

definitions.meaning: to put one's signature on something
Gemini, the Twins, is a star ... of the zodiac

explanation.definitionFit: To autograph is to write your name, and Gemini is one of the twelve zodiac emblems.

clue.text: Birds requiring drinks after dark

indicators.note: the drinks come after the dark in the answer, so the pieces join in that order

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day
a jar is British slang for a drink, usually of beer

explanation.surface: Some birds go out drinking once darkness falls.
explanation.walkthrough: A JAR is British slang for a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightjars are nocturnal insect-eating birds with a churring call.
